summary: The same egg-colouring activity occurs with I kṣuʕənne and III maṣuʕina; object semantics cannot decide the stem. The prefix and registered bases distinguish them.

Detransitive Preterit ṣwiʕi presents the coloured patient state in 112/334. The inherited Detransitive Infinitiv ṣwoʕo also functions as an ordinary active event noun; its box position is preserved without inferring a Detransitive event.
Body-part possessive objects (hands) and ruḥe reflexives retain active morphology. There is no evidence here for a distinct cosmetic, animal or reciprocal-wounding sense.

No new numbered senses or idioms. I Infectum-wa is genuinely absent after round 1, while I Infectum already has four examples. The occupational example incidentally supplies a fifth Infectum token without duplicating the quotation.

New nominal contexts justify revisiting round 1s retained Detransitive Infinitiv placement. ṣwoʕo is the active activity in du ṣwoʕo and with the genitive object in the existing boards quotation. Correct that one existing example and label new nominal examples Infinitiv; ṣwiʕi water colored by blood remains Detransitive Preterit.
Round 1 already moves the III egg quotation to Infectum and corrects Christmas to Easter. Jan confirms Easter egg coloring, but neither correction is repeated in entry.json.
Preserve ṣəwʕiwo, ṣuwaʕwo, ṣəwʕituwola and ṣwoʕaṯṯe as printed. They are not new dye senses, and color values do not justify altering the inherited red/white discrepancy without the edition.
111/38 has semoqo 'red', whereas the edition translation says weiß. Verify which colour the source intended; keep both supplied readings unchanged in the new quotation.
Reconcile the inherited NE_254;11 reference with supplied MAC NE interview 1/14 before changing citation metadata.

Confirm the editors intended ordinary Infinitiv placement for the active nominal ṣwoʕo, now supported by purpose and event-question uses, rather than a convention that puts all such nouns in the Detransitive subsection.
At 2.5/1613 does ṣwoʕo denote painting a picture or its paint/color? The fragment is not selected as an example.
Correct farben to färben
rationale: The verb meaning to dye is färben. The unaccented farben is an inherited typo, also present in the supplied corpus translation; the Turoyo ṣoʕət and the stem gloss färben establish the intended word.

summary: Eggs, yarn, hands, a fox and game knucklebones undergo colouring. Active ruḥo and reciprocal ḥḏoḏe change participant relations without creating a Detransitive form or a new lexical sense.
Reciprocal staining with blood in 60/25 parallels the existing I example; wounding is a contextual consequence, not a separate meaning of the colouring verb.
Jan occupational linen-dyeing and Easter eggs support existing I.1 and its round-1 participant extension. Result colors and l-marked beneficiaries/service areas do not create new senses.
